exposure: early postpartum lithium exposure through mother's milk
high serum lithium concentrations at birth (>=0.6 meq/l)
low serum lithium concentrations at birth (<0.6 meq/l)
cohort: The study included 25 infant-mother dyads where mothers were treated with lithium during and after pregnancy, and their infants were breastfed.
finding: High serum lithium concentration at birth was associated with an increased lithium level at follow-up and a higher rate of neonatal symptoms, suggesting late intrauterine lithium exposure might contribute to adverse effects in breastfed infants.
